subject.title: fix(sqlite): normalize BLOB/TEXT type mismatches during STRICT migration

question: For legacy BLOB/TEXT primary-key collisions that normalize to the same key, should OpenClaw ship an in-product non-destructive Doctor recovery before this migration repair lands, or intentionally retain a manual-recovery fail-closed path?
rationale: The collision represents ambiguous persisted user state: the implementation cannot safely choose which row to discard, while the affected upgrade path can otherwise remain blocked.

options.title: Add non-destructive Doctor recovery
options.body: Provide a visible recovery flow that preserves both conflicting records for operator resolution without silently choosing or deleting one.

options.title: Accept manual recovery
options.body: Retain the fail-closed migration error and explicitly document that conflicting legacy primary keys require operator database cleanup.

options.title: Pause this partial repair
options.body: Defer the change until the broader migration recovery policy for the related crash-loop report is settled.

recommendation.title: Add non-destructive Doctor recovery
recommendation.body: Provide a visible recovery flow that preserves both conflicting records for operator resolution without silently choosing or deleting one.

likelyOwner.reason: The affected STRICT migration originated in the SQLite safety work merged through commit 30ae21fca.
